title: Proteomic analysis of aqueous humor from patients with Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy reveals downregulated expression of HSP60
task: Identify differentially abundant proteins in aqueous humor from FECD patients
key_results: 455 proteins identified, 48 significantly downregulated in FECD vs controls; HSP60 reduction confirmed in aqueous humor and corneal endothelial tissue
comments: Proteomics alone cannot establish causation; HSP60 downregulation may be a consequence rather than driver of endothelial dysfunction in FECD.

model_io.model: Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)
inputs: aqueous humor samples from mild FECD patients
aqueous humor samples from advanced FECD patients
aqueous humor samples from control subjects

model_io.model: Validation by additional analysis

hypotheses.hypothesis: HSP60 expression is reduced in FECD aqueous humor compared to controls
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; HSP60 downregulation verified in both aqueous humor and tissue

hypotheses.hypothesis: Differentially expressed proteins associate with energy metabolism and cytoskeleton disorganization
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; functional enrichment analysis showed enrichment in these pathways

title: Machine learning identifies plasma-derived exosomal miRNAs associated with low muscle mass in Tibetan patients with rheumatoid arthritis
task: Identification of plasma exosomal miRNAs associated with low muscle mass in RA patients
key_results: 101 candidate dysregulated miRNAs identified (61 upregulated, 40 downregulated); hsa-miR-1294 and hsa-let-7c-5p prioritized; nomogram models achieve AUROC 0.905
comments: Study uses exploratory thresholds without FDR correction; results are hypothesis-generating and require validation in independent cohorts.

model_io.model: High-throughput miRNA sequencing + machine learning
miRNA-mRNA regulatory network analysis
miRNA and target gene-based nomogram models

hypotheses.hypothesis: Exosomal miRNAs regulate muscle mass through sphingolipid metabolism and oxidative phosphorylation
hypotheses.result: Functional enrichment identified nominally enriched metabolic pathways and immune cell infiltration differences

title: ConvSNN: an energy-efficient hybrid convolutional-spiking neural network for wrist-worn stress and affective state recognition
task: Energy-efficient stress and affective state recognition from wrist-worn sensors
key_results: 98.07% accuracy (random split), 94.0% LOSO accuracy, 48.31 μJ per-inference energy, expected calibration error reduced from 0.149 to 0.017
comments: Hybrid spiking neural networks offer promising energy efficiency for wearable deployment, though embedded hardware validation is still pending.

model_io.model: ConvSNN (4-stage 1D CNN + time-to-first-spike classification head)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hybrid CNN-SNN architecture balances accuracy and energy efficiency for wearable affective monitoring
hypotheses.result: 94.0% LOSO accuracy with 48.31 μJ per-inference energy enables smartwatch-class deployment

hypotheses.hypothesis: Temperature scaling improves probability calibration without sacrificing accuracy
hypotheses.result: ECE reduced from 0.149 to 0.017 with no accuracy change

title: Evaluating parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models for sentiment analysis with bayesian optimization
task: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning of LLMs for Arabic sentiment analysis
key_results: SILMA-9B-Instruct achieves F1-scores of 88.95% (ASTD), 89.91% (LABR), and 96.55% (HARD); LoRA with Bayesian optimization optimizes rank, dropout, and learning rate
comments: Application of existing PEFT techniques to sentiment analysis; Bayesian optimization for hyperparameter tuning is standard practice rather than methodological innovation.

model_io.model: LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, LLaMA-3-8B, SILMA-9B-Instruct
LoRA with Bayesian optimization

hypotheses.hypothesis: LoRA-based instruction-tuning can match sequence classification performance with fewer parameters
hypotheses.result: LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct achieves competitive F1-scores compared to LLaMA-3-8B with classification head

title: Comparative evaluation of statistical learning methods for polygenic prediction in UK Biobank
task: Comparative evaluation of polygenic risk score methods across genetic architectures
key_results: Non-infinitesimal models outperform infinitesimal when causal SNP proportion is low; SBayesRC and PolyPred achieve highest accuracy; functional annotations improve prediction
comments: Comprehensive simulation and validation study clarifies method selection guidelines, though optimal approach remains trait-dependent and context-specific.

model_io.model: Genome-wide simulation framework
PRS methods: LDpred2, PRS-CS, SBayesR, SBayesRC, PolyPred, MegaPRS

hypotheses.hypothesis: Non-infinitesimal models outperform infinitesimal models when causal SNP proportion is low
hypotheses.result: Simulations and UK Biobank analyses confirmed superior performance of non-infinitesimal approaches in sparse causal architectures

hypotheses.hypothesis: Functional annotation integration improves PRS prediction accuracy
hypotheses.result: SBayesRC and PolyPred with functional annotations achieved highest predictive performance across traits

title: A secure multilayer audio encryption scheme based on chain ring algebraic S-boxes, Rössler diffusion, and 4D hyperchaotic permutation
task: Secure multilayer audio encryption via chain-ring S-boxes, Rössler diffusion, and hyperchaotic permutation
key_results: S-boxes reach nonlinearity 112 with differential approximation probability 0.0148; encrypted audio entropy 15.8999 bits; NPCR 99.6783%, UACI 33.4%; 28-second file encrypted in 0.2855 s
comments: Thorough cryptanalytic evaluation using NIST and information-theoretic metrics; however, formal security proof against known-plaintext or chosen-ciphertext attacks is absent.

model_io.model: Three-stage encryption (Rössler XOR diffusion + 4D Lü hyperchaotic permutation + dual chain-ring S-box substitution)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dual independent chaotic systems (Rössler and 4D Lü) provide stronger confusion-diffusion than single chaotic source
hypotheses.result: Supported by high nonlinearity, entropy, and NPCR/UACI metrics; computational cost remains practical

title: Vehicle CO₂ emission prediction based on firefly with ant colony optimization tuned long short-term memory model
task: Predict vehicle CO₂ emissions from standard descriptors using FA–ACO–LSTM
key_results: FA–ACO–LSTM achieves R²=98.71%, MSE=0.0099, MAE=0.0791 on test set; outperforms FA–ACO–CNN (R²=93.55%), GRU, MLP, TabNet; excluding fuel-consumption features degrades R² to 88.08%
comments: Rigorous hyperparameter tuning and feature selection pipeline, but LSTM acts as feature-interaction learner on cross-sectional data, not true temporal forecasting; fuel-consumption proxies dominate predictions.

model_io.model: FA–ACO–LSTM (Firefly + Ant Colony Optimization tuned LSTM)
inputs: vehicle descriptors: engine size, cylinders, transmission, fuel consumption (COMB, HWY, COMB-mpg), etc. from Canadian registry (n=22,556)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Mixed-variable FA–ACO hyperparameter tuning improves LSTM from baseline R²=96.53% to 98.71% by optimizing learning dynamics
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 45% reduction in MSE; ANOVA confirms significance (F=30.2, p<0.0001)

title: Bifurcation analysis of continuous and discrete time predator-prey models with habitat complexity
task: Bifurcation analysis of predator-prey model with Holling Type II response and habitat complexity
key_results: Hopf and transcritical bifurcations characterized in continuous model; Neimark-Sacker bifurcation in discrete analog; Turing instability conditions derived
comments: Comprehensive analytical treatment of both continuous and discrete systems, but numerical bifurcation diagrams are not provided.

model_io.model: Continuous and discrete predator-prey systems (forward Euler discretization)
inputs: habitat complexity parameter; Holling Type II functional response coefficients

hypotheses.hypothesis: Habitat complexity induces additional bifurcations and alters stability regions
hypotheses.result: Supported by theoretical analysis and numerical validation

title: CFD-based recurrent neural network modeling of plasma-assisted flow control over a stepped NACA4412 airfoil using LSTM and GRU
task: Predict unsteady aerodynamic flow over stepped airfoil with plasma actuation
key_results: LSTM/GRU surrogate models accurately predict velocity fields; plasma + BFS achieved 83.07% lift improvement and 44.43% lift-to-drag enhancement
comments: CFD data-driven LSTM/GRU surrogate reduces computational cost, but direct comparison of prediction accuracy metrics against CFD baseline is not quantified.

model_io.model: LSTM and GRU recurrent networks
inputs: time-resolved CFD velocity field data from SST k–ω simulations at Re=3.1×10⁶

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dual AC-DBD plasma actuation delays boundary-layer separation and weakens vortical structures
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; 30%c BFS + plasma achieved maximum lift improvement of 83.07%

title: Two scale black holes with a phenomenological suppression profile: extremality, null critical curves, and test field spectra
task: Characterize extremal and spectral properties of two-scale black hole with phenomenological suppression
key_results: Ricci/Kretschmann scalars vanish at center; WKB frequencies match pseudospectral calculation within 0.22%; third-order WKB agrees with time-domain evolution to 0.48%
comments: High-precision analytical and numerical validation is provided, but physical interpretation of the suppression profile and observational signatures remain unexplored.

model_io.model: Two-scale black hole metric (Hayward + phenomenological suppression)
outputs: curvature scalars, null critical curve, quasinormal mode frequencies

hypotheses.hypothesis: Suppression factor regularizes curvature singularities while preserving C⁴ Cartesian extension
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; Ricci and Kretschmann vanish at center with bounded orthonormal components

title: Novel adaptive fixed-time synchronization for fractional-order uncertain Hopfield neural networks with proportional delays of unbounded nature
task: Fixed-time synchronization of fractional-order Hopfield neural networks with unbounded proportional delays
key_results: Novel adaptive multi-module controller achieves fixed-time synchronization; settling time governed by control parameters and can be estimated a priori
comments: Theoretical framework is rigorous, but no numerical examples demonstrating settling-time estimates or robustness to parameter uncertainty are included.

model_io.model: Adaptive controller for fractional-order uncertain Hopfield neural networks
inputs: master neural state, proportional delay τ(t)=θt with θ∈(0,1)
outputs: synchronization error convergent to zero in fixed time

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-module adaptive control (negative feedback + delay suppression + convergence enhancement) enables fixed-time synchronization despite unbounded delays
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by Lyapunov analysis; settling time depends on control parameter tuning

title: A hybrid memetic algorithm for an energy-aware distributed blocking hybrid flowshop scheduling problem with transportation time
task: Optimize distributed hybrid flowshop scheduling with energy and transportation time
key_results: Hybrid memetic algorithm (HMA) achieves competitive makespan and energy minimization on 100 benchmark instances
comments: Mathematical model and HMA design are presented, but no numerical tables comparing HMA performance against recent algorithms quantitatively.

model_io.model: Hybrid Memetic Algorithm (HMA) with adaptive local search
inputs: job count, stage count, factory count; energy consumption, transportation time parameters
outputs: job schedule minimizing makespan and total energy

hypotheses.hypothesis: Neighborhood strategy tailored to energy saving reduces redundant consumption without sacrificing makespan
hypotheses.result: Supported by experimental results, but specific quantitative trade-offs not detailed

title: A drift adaptive framework for detecting and tracking evolving anomalies in financial transaction streams
task: Detect and track evolving anomalies in financial transaction streams under concept drift
key_results: HADA+ achieves ROC-AUC=0.915219±0.000954, PR-AUC=0.068736±0.000436 on Credit Card Fraud; five-event macro-F1=0.9673 on Controlled Lifecycle Validation (vs. 0.3674 nearest-centroid)
comments: Framework preserves lifecycle continuity and handles drift well, but low PR-AUC and Precision@100 suggest high false-positive rate in production deployment.

model_io.model: HADA+ (Adaptive Anomaly Prioritization + Score-Aware Clustering + Optimal Transport Lifecycle Alignment + Lifecycle Evolution Modeling)
inputs: transaction stream with evolving concept drift, lifecycle events
outputs: anomaly score, priority class, lifecycle event classification

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cross-window optimal-transport alignment and lifecycle modeling preserve structural anomaly populations across drift
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; Evolution Continuity Score=0.755973±0.000886 demonstrates drift-responsive tracking

title: A multi-task deep learning network for robust and high accuracy star sensor image centroiding
task: Sub-pixel star centroid estimation from noisy sensor imagery
key_results: 100.0% binary-star detection rate (vs. 53.7% conventional); 0.017-pixel centroid error under non-Gaussian conditions (vs. 0.16 pixels conventional)
comments: Multi-task CNN cleverly decouples classification and regression with Pareto loss, but deployment validation on actual flight hardware remains absent.

model_io.model: HorNet-based lightweight multi-task CNN
inputs: star sensor images with Gaussian, non-Gaussian, and binary-star profiles

hypotheses.hypothesis: Differentiable Gaussian convolution + coordinate attention improve robustness to non-Gaussian morphologies
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; achieved 0.017-pixel error vs. 0.12 pixels for Gaussian fitting

title: Infrared quantum emission and its tuning from boron-nitride nanotube fluors
task: Engineer tunable infrared quantum emission from defect-based boron-nitride nanotubes
key_results: DFT predicts tunable zero-phonon-line emission 1000–2000 nm via diameter variation (0.4–0.8 nm); CB defects in (5,0) BNNT tunable 2000–2300 nm under strain and 2000–3400 nm under electric field
comments: First-principles predictions span telecommunications C/L-bands and beyond; however, experimental validation of predicted quantum emission and excited-state dynamics is essential before deployment.

model_io.model: Single-walled BNNT with intrinsic point defects

hypotheses.hypothesis: Point defects in BNNTs produce tunable near- and mid-infrared emission modulated by curvature, strain, and electric field
hypotheses.result: Calculated emission ranges 980–4000 nm for CNVB and 1800–2300 nm for VB; CB defect covers 1000–3400 nm spectrum

title: A single passive terahertz metasurface implementing eight Boolean logic gates through polarization multiplexing
task: Implement eight Boolean logic gates on single passive terahertz metasurface via polarization multiplexing
key_results: Eight gates (OR, AND, XOR, BUFFER, NOR, NAND, XNOR, NOT) on 16λ₀×16λ₀ aperture; mean detector contrast 13.22 dB, minimum 5.88 dB; correct routing for all 28 gate-input combinations
comments: Polarization multiplexing doubles functional density using passive phase-tuning via geometric parameters; scalability to larger gate counts and robustness against fabrication variations deserve further investigation.

model_io.model: Transmissive terahertz metasurface with gold-on-polyimide crossed resonant arms
outputs: logical output (whichever window has higher energy)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Orthogonal x- and y-polarization channels carrying independent Rayleigh-Sommerfeld phase profiles enable simultaneous gate and complement operation
hypotheses.result: Eight distinct logic gates plus complements successfully routed with 13.22 dB mean contrast on single passive metasurface

title: Hybrid plasmonic–photonic multi-Fano resonance refractive index sensor using periodic gold nano-bar assisted microcavity coupling
task: Design multi-Fano resonance refractive index sensor using hybrid plasmonic-photonic structures
key_results: Sensitivity of 975 nm/RIU and figure of merit of 139.28 at Mode 5; excellent linear wavelength-to-refractive-index dependence enabling high-resolution biochemical sensing
comments: The multi-mode capability and geometric tunability are advantageous, though fabrication tolerances of nano-scale features remain a practical concern.

model_io.model: Hybrid plasmonic-photonic microcavity with periodic gold nano-bars

hypotheses.hypothesis: Sharp Fano resonances emerge from coupling periodic gold nano-bars with dielectric micro-cavity
hypotheses.result: Multi-Fano response confirmed via electric field distributions showing hybrid plasmon-cavity modes
